steps.text: Bring broth, water, pork chops, soy sauce, paprika, oregano, garlic powder, salt, pepper, chili powder, and bay leaf to a boil, uncovered, in a large stockpot over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 1 hour, then remove from the heat. Transfer 3/4 cup cooking broth to a 2-cup liquid measure. Transfer pork chops to a cutting board to cool, about 20 minutes.
Whisk flour into reserved cooking liquid and set aside. Remove and discard bones from cooled pork chops. Shred meat or chop into bite-sized pieces.
Add potato, broccoli, carrot, onion, celery, and cooked pork to the stockpot and bring to a boil. Stir in flour mixture, reduce the heat, and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove and discard bay leaf, then gently mash potatoes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Chop Soup
raw_recipe.description: This easy pork soup starts with slow-simmered pork chops that are shredded and cooked with a hearty mixture of potatoes and other vegetables.

review.reviewBody: This was FABULOUS! I made some slight variations but didn't change too much: I thought it would make a better stew than a soup, so I only used 1 - 1/2 cups of chicken broth rather than 3 cups. Also, I used bok choy instead of broccoli. I love broccoli but it has such a strong flavor on its own and I thought this recipe could use something more subtle.

I was missing some ingredients so I substituted some beef rib bone broth from the other night, and tried worcestershire sauce in place of soy (it worked well!), left out broccoli, bay leaves, and celery, and doubled the garlic and salt as is standard in this kitchen. It was delicious. I found that it was ready before the cook time was up. 40 minutes on the second cooking was more than enough. Had to order myself to not go for 3rds so this is definitely a winner.

The soup benefited by browning the pork chops first. This left a nice fond in the fry pan. I added some chicken broth and the flour to the fry pan and mixed to dissolve the flour, but I did NOT heat it. Everything added to the pot 1 hour before the meal except for the flour slurry, pork chops and broccoli. After 1/2 hour, add the above and simmer for another half hour. Then remove the bay leaf and chops. Dice up the meat and add back to the pot. I found that it was best not to overcook the meat and broccoli. I also used 2 potatoes instead of three.

Great soup! I used leftovers from Pork Picnic Pot Roast on this site. I cooked the broccoli in the broth from the pot roast and added in the spices and one can of chicken broth and one can of corn and the leftover potatoes, carrots, and celery. I mixed the flour with about a half a cup of water and added it but that was the only extra water I added. It turned out great!

I had to add more liquid, it simmered down a lot. I read a review that suggested leaving out the soy sauce so, I left that out. I salted and peppered the pork chops and browned them first. I didn't mash the potatoes, just left them as they were. It was a delicious outcome and both my husband and I loved it. I will make it again!

I used the crock pot. So I put the spices (all but used 1 tsp of onion powder instead of onions) and boneless, defatted pork chops in the crock with 5 cups of chicken broth until the meat was fork tender. (3 hrs on high) Then I pulled the pork out and shredded it a bit with a forks. I reserved the broth and added the flour, as the recipe called. Chopped all veggies as called for, then added the rewhisked broth and flour when it got bubbly. All in all it took about 5 hours in the crock pot. Everyone was salivating the entire time it was cooking. Excellent recipe!
Thanks for the dinner Idea, instead using chicken stock I made my own pork stock using pork neck bones, and I topped it with smoked pork tenderloin. It was delicious.

I marinated the pork in crushed pineapple chunks and olive oil with spices before pouring all of it into the pot for the first hour. The pineapple chunks were removed after 1 hour. 
I did not use chicken broth or soy sauce or flour for health reasons. 
I added spinach during the second hour. 
The pork was sliced thin and it was very soft. Pepper and chili couldn't be tasted at all. I will try to make the soup hotter next time.

My husband smoke/grilled a large pork butt and we had leftovers so I didn't use pork chops. I added already cooked pork, all the ingredients (I didn't have celery and I chopped up some small red and white potatoes) and a can of chopped green chilies into my Instant Pot. I set it to high pressure for 10 minutes with a 10 minute slow release. I stirred in 2-3 handfuls of mixed greens when I removed the lid to boost the nutritional value. Dinner in less than 30 minutes! 

Note to self: Since I had to use Better Than Bouillon (we were out of homemade chicken stock) and the pork was already seasoned, I should have left out the added salt as it is just a tad too salty.

I have nothing but high praises for this delicious soup. It would have been perfect just the way it was presented, and the only reason I made any changes at all was because I used what I had on hand without having to make a trip to the store. I had a bag of stew vegetables and three boneless pork chops that needed to be cooked. I put those in to Allrecipes' search engine, and VOILA! No broccoli in the fridge, but extra celery and some minced garlic. I also cut the meat in advance and browned it in my Dutch oven, just to avoid extra dishes. But, that's really about all I did differently. This soup turned out amazing. And, it made the whole house smell so good while it was cooking, my mouth was literally watering as I ladled in my first bowl! It's definitely a keeper, and one I'll fix again to share with friends and family.

It was okay. Nothing special. Made my own pork bone broth instead of using chicken broth and didn’t mash the potatoes, otherwise followed recipe. It’s a good way to stretch a couple of pork chops, but nothing I’ll likely make again.

The soup came out great. The only thing I would change is leave the salt out of the recipe. I used low sodium chicken broth and it still came out salty with the amount of salt called for in the recipe.

This is the perfect recipe for leftover smoked pork shoulder (pulled pork!) I think I've made this before with leftover pork chops, but I didn't see my review. This is very good and different. The only changes I made were the type of pork and I sauteed the onions, carrots and celery up front. Left out the salt and the seasonings were perfect. Thanks for the recipe!

Fantastic!!! I love reading recipes and this recipe is why I’m glad I do. I never heard of pork chop soup before, but it sounded delicious with all the vegetables in it. The pork added the protein necessary to get me through a 12 hour shift. I cut the meat off the bone, but I cooked them as well for the nutrition. The seasonings are just right. I added a little extra because I added more broth. I dredged my chops in flour seasoned with salt and pepper and browned them in EVOO before adding to broth to cook. I didn’t use the soy sauce. Next time I’ll use red potatoes as the russet became slightly mushy. Just an excellent recipe!

Wow! Incredible soup! I did sear the pork chops first before adding stock. Didn't use broccoli, and sautéed the veggies (except potatoes) before adding to the soup for max flavour! It was amazing! The whole family loved it!
Awesome! Simple ingredients and very tasty

I follow the recipe, almost exact, cut back on oregano and chili powder to 1/4 tsp, minced garlic instead of garlic powder and no bay leaf. I mashed about half of the potatoes. The flavor was very rich and tasty. I would make it again.
Mine came out a dark broth from the soya sauce not the colour in your picture! I added real grated ginger and real garlic. Very good soup.
Very good yes I did make changes. My pork chops I had them them the other night and I cut them up and added them at the beginning and they were delicious.
It came out perfect. I didn’t have broccoli or celery so i used zucchini and cabbage and added red onions too. It still came out great.
